longForms:
A few units people confuse:

- density: kg/m³
- pressure: Pa (not bar)
- force: N
- energy: J

> The SI unit of density is kilogram per cubic metre.

Pretty much what the syllabus says, see 021.08.

Worked example:

```
m = 1.225 kg
V = 1 m³
ρ = m / V = 1.225 kg/m³
```

Useful table:

| Quantity | SI unit |
| --- | --- |
| density | kg/m³ |
| pressure | Pa |
| force | N |
See the [SI brochure](https://www.bipm.org/en/measurement-units) for the official definitions.
I wrote a short summary: **density** goes down with altitude, which is why *true airspeed* is higher than *indicated airspeed* when you climb.
